Welcome to Cross in Hand Church of England Primary School
Learning together,Growing together
A caring Church of England School where every child flourishes academically, socially and spiritually.
Welcome
Cross in Hand Church of England Primary School is a deeply inclusive and welcoming school, driven by a vision that ensures every child and adult can flourish.
Our dedicated staff team is committed to nurturing the whole child, providing an inspiring environment where spiritual and academic growth go hand-in-hand. We strive to offer a transformative learning experience rooted in dignity and respect, and we hope this website captures the community and joy that defines our school family.
If you would like to find out more about Cross in Hand Church of England Primary School please contact the school office 01435 862941.
Open Events
Monday 16th November 6.30pm
Tuesday 17th November 9.15am
To apply for a place please follow this link.
Deadline for applications on 15th January 2027
Please contact the office if you can't make any of these times.
School Values
Cross in Hand Church of England Primary School has established Respect, Community, Kindness, and Perseverance as its four core Christian values to provide a moral and spiritual compass that guides every aspect of school life.
By weaving these specific values into the curriculum and daily interactions, the school provides practical, life-enhancing force that drives both academic achievement and personal wellbeing.
Enrichment Fridays
At Cross in Hand Church of England Primary School, we are passionate about providing children with a broad, balanced and inspiring curriculum. As part of this commitment, our Year 5 and Year 6 pupils take part in Enrichment Fridays, a dedicated afternoon designed to celebrate creativity, develop new skills and nurture individual talents.
Breakfast ClubStart the day with a healthy breakfast and supervised activities before school opens each morning.
Activity ClubsExplore our wide range of extracurricular enrichment clubs including sport, creative arts and hobbies.
After School ClubReliable wrap-around childcare providing games, outdoor play, and snacks after the school day ends.
Thrive
Thrive Approach is a tangible expression of "Dignity and Respect," as it treats each child as a unique individual made in the image of God, providing bespoke support. It bridges the gap between the school's theological values and practical mental health support.
The Thrive ApproachAt its heart, the Thrive Approach encourages adults - parents, carers, and teachers - to understand the emotional needs of others.
Meet the Thrive TeamMeet the staff members who make up our Thrive team working together ever day to support children on their journey.
Why is sport important?Discover how physical education and team sports build resilience, teamwork, and healthy lifelong habits.
SwimmingExplore our swimming program, helping children develop water confidence, safety skills, and stroke technique.
DanceLearn about our creative dance opportunities that encourage self-expression, rhythm, coordination, and performance skills.
Year 3 & 4 ProductionExplore photos, performance details, and highlights from out Lower Key Stage 2 annual theatrical production.
Year 5 & 6 ProductionDiscover the showcase production from our Upper Key Stage 2 pupils celebrating talent, acting, and musical achievements.
School GovernorsMeet our Governing Body, responsible for providing strategic leadership, accountability, and oversight for Cross in Hand Primary School.
Friends of Cross in HandDiscover our active parent-teacher association (PTA), bringing the community together through fun events and vital fundraising projects.
Year 6 Residential
Our Year 6 residential was more than just a trip; it was an opportunity for our pupils to build a supportive community rooted in hope and perseverance. From the quiet moments of reflection to the exhilaration of the high-ropes, we witnessed our children growing in character and resilience.

School Vision
Sharing a whole‑school vision based on John 10:10, “life in all its fullness,” helps children understand the deeper purpose behind their learning and daily choices. It encourages them to see school not just as a place for academic progress, but as a community where they can grow emotionally, socially, and spiritually.
When this message was explored in assembly, it became something the whole school reflects on together, creating unity and a shared sense of direction. It inspired our children to use their gifts, care for others, and approach each day with curiosity, gratitude, and a desire to flourish.
Self Identity
Teaching children about self‑identity helps them understand who they are beyond external expectations. When children explore their interests, values, and cultural roots, they develop a grounded sense of belonging and direction. This clarity strengthens confidence, guiding them as they make choices and form relationships. A strong self‑identity also supports emotional wellbeing, because children learn to appreciate their uniqueness rather than compare themselves to others. It encourages empathy too, as understanding themselves helps them respect differences in others. Nurturing self‑identity early lays the foundation for children to grow into secure, self‑aware, and authentic individuals.
Self Worth
Teaching children about self‑worth gives them a foundation that shapes how they navigate the world. When kids understand their value, they’re more likely to set healthy boundaries, make confident decisions, and resist negative pressures. It helps them develop resilience, because they learn that mistakes don’t diminish their worth. A strong sense of self also supports emotional wellbeing, encouraging them to build positive relationships and treat others with respect. Ultimately, nurturing self‑worth early on empowers children to grow into secure, compassionate, and self‑assured adults.
Self Belief
Teaching children about self‑belief gives them the inner strength to face challenges with courage rather than fear. When kids trust their abilities, they’re more willing to try new things, persist through setbacks, and develop a healthy sense of independence. Self‑belief nurtures motivation, helping them see effort as a path to growth rather than something to avoid. It also supports emotional resilience, allowing them to bounce back when things don’t go as planned. By fostering self‑belief early, we equip children with the confidence to pursue their goals and shape their own futures with optimism and determination.
Race Awareness Week
Teaching children about Race Awareness Week helps them understand the diverse world they live in and encourages them to appreciate differences rather than fear them. When kids learn about race in an open, age‑appropriate way, they become more empathetic, more aware of unfair treatment, and more confident in challenging prejudice.
It also gave us the language to talk about identity and inclusion, which strengthens our social and emotional development. By introducing these ideas early, we help our children build respectful relationships, celebrate cultural diversity, and grow into adults who value equality and fairness.

Vision, Values and Aims
Vision
At Cross in Hand Church of England Primary school, we enable each child to thrive, helping them to develop to their full potential within a caring community and an engaging environment. We provide an education of the highest standard built upon the foundations of our strong Christian values and a desire to make learning fun.
Values
Ephesians 4:32 – “Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other, just as in Christ God forgave you.”
Romans 12:4-5 - "For just as each of us has one body with many members, and these members do not all have the same function, so in Christ we, though many, form one body, and each member belongs to all the others."
Philippians 2:3-4 - "Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves, not looking to your own interests but each of you to the interests of the others."
Romans 5:3-4 - "Not only so, but we also glory in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope."
Aims
Provide a broad, balanced and creative curriculum

Welcome to Cross in Hand Church of England Primary School
At Cross in Hand CofE Primary School, our Christian foundation shapes everything we do. We are proud to be a Church of England school where Christian values aren't just words on a wall – they're lived out every day in our classrooms, playground, and wider community.
Educating the Whole Child
We believe education is about much more than academic achievement. While we're committed to helping every child reach their full potential in their learning, we recognise that spiritual growth is equally important. Our approach nurtures:
Spiritual development – helping children explore faith, meaning and purpose
Moral development – building strong character and understanding of right and wrong
Social development – learning to work together, show respect and build friendships
Cultural development – appreciating diversity and different perspectives
This holistic approach is woven throughout our carefully planned curriculum, ensuring every child develops as a well-rounded individual.
Our Christian Values in Action
Our Christian ethos is expressed through four core values that guide everything we do:
These values connect directly to our school vision – find out more on our Vision and Values page.
Part of the Church of England Family
Church of England schools offer a distinctively Christian education. While each church school is unique, we all share core values rooted in the Gospel. At Cross in Hand, loving God and loving our neighbours isn't just an aspiration – it's how we live together every day.
We aim to serve our community by providing the highest quality education within the context of Christian belief and practice.
We encourage all our pupils to:
Understand the meaning and significance of faith
Experience Christian values in action
Develop their own spiritual awareness
We have more information on our R.E Curriculum page under our curriculum tab, you can also access this page.
Our Diocesan Links
We are proud members of the Diocese of Chichester family of schools, which provides support, guidance and a network of fellow church schools.
As a Voluntary Controlled Church of England Primary School, we maintain close links with our local church community and the wider Anglican family.

Clubs
At Cross in Hand we aim to provide a range of clubs during term time. Whilst some may run throughout the year, others may only run for a specified time. We would encourage all pupils to participate and try the clubs on offer. Most clubs offered are organised by outside agencies while some teachers have their own areas of expertise and interest and offer additional opportunities for pupils in these areas.
When the children join a club, we expect commitment from them and if they cannot attend, it is their responsibility to notify the teacher running the club. If a child decides they do not want to continue with a club, they should also tell the teacher to allow that space to be taken by another child as there is often a waiting list. We expect the same high standards of behaviour in clubs as we do in school and so we make pupils aware that if their behaviour falls short of this, they may lose their space and their parents will be notified.
A letter about clubs on offer is sent out at the start of each term.

Welcome to Cross in Hand Church of England Primary School
Yoto Project
Reading sits at the heart of every child’s learning journey. Strong reading skills open the door to the full curriculum, building confidence, curiosity, and a lifelong love of learning. From the earliest years, we prioritise creating joyful, meaningful reading experiences for all our pupils.
Our Yoto Project brings this vision to life by pairing older and younger children through the magic of storytelling. Older pupils record captivating audio versions of favourite books, which are then turned into bespoke Yoto cards. Younger children listen to these recordings while following along in their own copies, strengthening both comprehension and enthusiasm for reading.
To ensure everyone in Reception, Year 1 & Year 2 can take part, Yoto players and book sets rotate around the children. This simple but powerful routine helps foster connection, independence, and a shared love of stories throughout our school community.
Reception, Year 1 & Year 2
Children will take it in turn to take home the Yoto player and the books and they will be able to listen to older children reading their favourite stories as the follow along in the books.
Thanks to the Friends of Cross in Hand School for funding this project.
